Observational studies enable the examination of how students actually use the 
application. This approach unveils how the user reacts to the gamified features 
and short-form content, thus offering insights into their engagement. However, 
the limited control over environmental variables, and the likelihood of observer 
biases, may hinder the effectiveness and causative relationships between the 
applications features and student outcomes. 
Considering the given constraints and the aims of this study, a hybrid approach 
seems most suitable, integrating observational studies, a structured survey post 
usage, and an examination to gauge recall. This methodology blends the 
observations of the tutor with the self-reported experience from the student, 
thus mitigating any individual biases, while ensuring that the perceived learning 
is empirical. The observational phase of the study is designed to capture student 
reactions to features, while focusing on the student’s engagement and 
distractibility levels. Once completed, a structured survey will delve deeper into 
the student’s, usability, motivation, and future use intent; attempting to prompt 
the student to take a more holistic view, followed by a short examination to 
measure the students content mastery and understanding.
